title: Chicken Chasni
subtitle: A sweet and tangy Scottish-Indian curry with a vibrant pink sauce
excerpt: Tender chicken thighs in a lightly spiced sauce that balances sweet mango chutney against sharp lemon juice. A Scottish-Indian restaurant classic with a vivid colour.
sourceNotes: Chasni is a creation of the Scottish-Indian restaurant scene; the name comes from the Urdu word for sugar syrup, reflecting its sweet-sour character.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool and freeze in portions for up to three months. Defrost overnight and reheat in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the quantity easily. Use two pans side by side rather than overcrowding one.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook up to a day ahead. The sauce becomes more complex after a night in the fridge.

content.text: Chasni sauce is pink, sweet and gently spiced. It is not a complex curry. The balance between the mango chutney and the lemon juice is the key thing to get right. Taste and adjust before serving.
Heat the oil in a wide saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until soft and turning gold.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for two minutes. Add the paprika, turmeric, cumin and tomato puree. Cook for two minutes more.
Add the blended tinned tomatoes and the mango chutney. Stir well and bring to a steady simmer. Cook for five minutes.
Add the chicken pieces and stir to coat in the sauce. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cooked through.
Pour in the cream and stir. Simmer for five minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Add the lemon juice and garam masala. Taste and add more chutney if you want it sweeter, or more lemon if you want it sharper.
Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with rice or naan.

items.cause: Too much mango chutney relative to the tomatoes.
items.fix: Add lemon juice a teaspoon at a time until the balance shifts. A small pinch of salt also cuts sweetness.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The chicken released too much water, or the cream was added too early.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for five to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Add the cream at the end only.

items.cause: The pieces were too small or cooked at too high a heat.
items.fix: Cut thighs into pieces no smaller than 3cm. Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil.
